subject: Maths
title: Angles in parallel lines
subtitle: Angles · KS3 Maths
learning_objective: I can identify and calculate alternate, corresponding and co-interior angles in parallel lines.

key_vocab.definition: When a transversal crosses two parallel lines, special angle pairs are formed: alternate, corresponding, and co-interior angles.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can identify and calculate alternate, corresponding and co-interior angles in parallel lines.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: transversal -- When a transversal crosses two parallel lines, special angle pairs are formed: alternate, corresponding, and co-interior angles.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Look for the Z, F, or C/U shape to identify the angle relationship. Then use equal or sum to 180°.
Alternate = equal; Co-interior = 180°
Z = equal, F = equal, C = 180°

Key examples:
  ✓ Alternate angles are equal  (Z-angles)
  ✓ Corresponding angles are equal  (F-angles)
  ✓ Co-interior angles sum to 180°  (C/U-angles)
  ✗ Co-interior angles are equal  (they sum to 180°)
  ✗ Alternate angles add to 180°  (they are equal)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – alternate angles
  Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle is 65°. Find the alternate angle.
  Identify the Z-shape
  Alternate angles are equal
  The angle = 65°
  = 65°
  (Alternate angles are always equal when lines are parallel.)

Example 2 – corresponding angles
  A transversal crosses parallel lines. One angle is 110°. Find the corresponding angle.
  Identify the F-shape
  Corresponding angles are equal
  The angle = 110°
  = 110°
  (Corresponding angles are in the same position at each intersection.)

sections.title: Alternate angles (Z)
sections.content:
Find the marked angle. Lines are parallel.

(a) Alternate to 55°
(b) Alternate to 120°
(c) Alternate to 83°
(d) Alternate to 145°

sections.title: Corresponding angles (F)
sections.content:
Find the corresponding angle.

(a) Corresponding to 70°
(b) Corresponding to 95°
(c) Corresponding to 132°
(d) Corresponding to 48°

sections.title: Co-interior angles (C/U)
sections.content:
Find the co-interior angle. They sum to 180°.

(a) Co-interior with 60°
(b) Co-interior with 115°
(c) Co-interior with 78°
(d) Co-interior with 143°

sections.title: Finding unknowns
sections.content:
Find the value of x.

(a) x and 2x are alternate angles
(b) x and (180 − x) are co-interior
(c) 2x + 10 and 70 are corresponding
(d) 3x and 2x + 40 are alternate

sections.title: Mixed angle problems
sections.content:
State the relationship and find the missing angle.

(a) Angle a is alternate to 74°
(b) Angle b is co-interior with 105°
(c) Angle c is corresponding to 138°
(d) x and 4x − 20 are co-interior; find x
(e) 2x + 15 and 3x − 10 are alternate; find x

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ Alternate angles are equal
✗ Co-interior angles are equal
✓ Corresponding angles are equal
✗ Alternate angles add to 180°
✓ These rules only work with parallel lines
